record.context_brief: Inverse correlation length versus free energy
record.original_question: In the localized phase, let μ(λ,h) denote the inverse correlation length defined through the exponential decay rate appearing in the model's excursion and correlation estimates. As h approaches the critical point h_c(λ) from below, is log μ(λ,h) asymptotic to log F(λ,h), where F(λ,h) is the free energy?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the copolymer model at a selective interface defined as follows. Let ω = (ω_n)_{n≥1} be a sequence of i.i.d. real random variables with mean zero, unit variance, and finite exponential moments, defined on a probability space with expectation E. Let S = (S_n)_{n≥0} be a simple symmetric random walk on Z, independent of ω, with law P and expectation E. For parameters λ > 0 and h ≥ 0, define the quenched partition function
   Z_{N,ω} = E[ exp( -2λ Σ_{n=1}^{N} (ω_n + h) Δ_n ) ],
where Δ_n = (1 - sign(S_n))/2 (taken to be (1 - sign(S_{n-1}))/2 when S_n = 0, by convention), so the polymer is penalized for monomers in the lower half-plane.

The quenched free energy is
   F(λ,h) = lim_{N→∞} (1/N) E[ log Z_{N,ω} ],
which exists and is non-negative. The critical curve is h_c(λ) = inf{h ≥ 0 : F(λ,h) = 0}, separating the localized phase {F > 0} from the delocalized phase {F = 0}.

For (λ,h) in the localized phase, define the inverse correlation length
   μ(λ,h) = - lim_{N→∞} (1/N) log E[ (1 + exp(-2λ Σ_{n=1}^{N}(ω_n + h))) / Z_{N,ω} ],
which governs the exponential decay rate of excursion and correlation estimates for the model.

Question: Is it true that
   log μ(λ,h)  ∼  log F(λ,h)   as  h ↗ h_c(λ),
in the sense that the ratio log μ(λ,h) / log F(λ,h) tends to 1?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether log μ(λ,h) is asymptotically equivalent to log F(λ,h) as h approaches the critical curve from the localized side is posed as a problem expected (in connection with disorder relevance) to fail, but no proof or disproof appears in the literature on copolymer models at selective interfaces. Subsequent work (e.g., Bolthausen–den Hollander–Opoku 2015) addresses variational characterizations of the free energy but does not resolve this asymptotic comparison.

status_evidence.title: A copolymer near a selective interface: Variational characterization of the free energy
status_evidence.snippet: Variational formula for the free energy of the copolymer near a selective interface, but does not establish the asymptotics of the inverse correlation length versus the free energy near criticality.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on copolymer free energy does not address the inverse correlation length asymptotics.

status_evidence.title: Copolymers at Selective Interfaces: Settled Issues and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey lists the comparison of log μ and log F near the critical point as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The comparison is identified as an unresolved problem in the copolymer literature.
